Actor Kevin Sorbo is facing heat on social media for a post saying Muslims shouldn’t be allowed to serve in public office.

“The phrase ‘Muslim elected official’ should not exist in America,” Sorbo, best known for playing the title role in the 1990s action series “Hercules,” wrote Sunday on X, where he has become a right-wing media personality.

But as many were quick to point out, that notion is in direct conflict with the U.S. Constitution, which plainly states that “no religious Test shall ever be required as a Qualification to any Office or public Trust under the United States.”

Sorbo, ironically, has also had strong feelings about people who don’t like what’s in the Constitution.

“If you hate the constitution, leave,” he wrote in 2020. “Go to another country that doesn’t have the same rights as America. Don’t destroy our country.”
